brief: UBS argues the Fed's 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% should not derail the equity rally despite a hawkish, unanimous vote. Sixteen of 18 officials see one more hike this year, up from half in June, but markets had priced four hikes over the cycle versus UBS's forecast of two, and UBS expects one further 25bp move this year. The initial reaction, a 13bp jump in the 2-year yield and lower equities, was contained by Wednesday's close: S&P 500 -0.4%, 2-year yield +1bp. Economic strength should let the market absorb tightening: the Fed raised its GDP forecasts, cut unemployment projections, and retail sales beat expectations. UBS forecasts S&P earnings growth of 25% in 2026 and 14% in 2027, arguing a harder equity environment needs higher yields plus weaker earnings and wider credit spreads together, so it stays positioned for gains while bracing for volatility and recommends diversification. Separately, UK inflation rose to 3.1% ahead of the BoE decision, but UBS expects a hold at 3.75% and stays bullish GBP, thinking market pricing overstates UK tightening. Japan is weighing a defense target of 3-3.5% of GDP, denied by its ministry; UBS blames the JGB yield rise on global yields and BOJ bets.
